newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty eases vs basket, T/N depos rise.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty eases vs basket, T/N depos rise.

text.p: The Polish zloty weakened slightly against the basket of currencies in light trade on client-driven currency purchases and banks extending currency exposure, dealers said.
They said players cut currency positions on Wednesday to gain on profitable zloty positions over the weekend but that they rebuldt them on Thursday.

"The zloty eased slightly today as banks rebuild currency positions cut on Wednesday, but any further losses should be limited by foreign investors who still have to pay for fixed bonds," said Bogdan Stepkowski from ING Bank in Warsaw.

The zloty closed at 2.92/2.87 percent from the trading band centre, weaker than Wednesday's close at 3.07/3.02 percent. It closed at 3.0885/05 to the dollar, down from 3.0780/95 on Wednesday and at 1.7970/78 to the mark, down from 1.7965/75.
Foreign investors who bought an estimated $40 million of fixed bonds on Wednesday will pay for it before March 12.
A source, which asked not to be named, said on Thursday the finance ministry had offered to sell T-bills directly to the central bank. It has not disclosed the amount of the deal.
The finance ministry and the central bank declined to confirm or deny that the offer had been made.
Despite the sale, which had no immediate effect on the secondary T-bill market, yields were still above the last primary auction's levels, dealers said.
They said Polish T-bill yields, which rose a point over the last month, could still grow to about 21.30 percent, despite the treasury's T-bill sale to the central bank.
Overnight deposit rates inched up to 21.65/21.85 percent from 21.65/21.75 percent this morning, tomorrow/next rose to 21.74/21.99 percent from Wednesday's 21.65/21.85 percent.
